content.title: Where to watch 76ers vs. Celtics: NBA Playoffs TV schedule, free live stream
content.text: Boston Celtics' Jaylen Brown (7) tries to get a shot past Philadelphia 76ers' Tyrese Maxey during the first half of an NBA basketball game Tuesday, Nov. 11, 2025, in Philadelphia. (AP Photo/Matt Rourke)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Joey Aliberti | JAliberti@syracuse.comThe Boston Celtics will face the Philadelphia 76ers in the first round of the NBA Playoffs, with Game 1 set for Sunday at 1 p.m. ET. Here’s everything you need to know to watch all the games of their first round series. Where can I stream 76ers vs. Celtics for free?The 76ers vs. Celtics series will air on various channels and stream live on DIRECTV, which offers a free trial.Game 3 will also stream exclusively on Amazon Prime Video (free trial). Game 2 and Game 4 will have streams available on Peacock. DIRECTVStream your favorite sports, and enjoy your first five days completely free. Plus, take $35 off your first month when you sign up today.Start for $0What channel is 76ers vs. Celtics on?The series will air on multiple channels, including ABC and NBC and NBCSN. Channels and streaming services are only listed for the first four games of the series, so there’s a chance of ESPN airing games later on in the series as well. NBC, ABC and ESPN will serve as the channels for all first round NBA Playoff games, with Prime Video taking exclusive rights to some games as well. DIRECTV (free trial) is the best way to watch the first round action. They have NBC, ABC and ESPN. You’ll also need a subscription to Prime Video for some of the games, which you can watch with a free trial. Peacock will also air Game 2, and will have a stream for the NBC games as well. 76ers vs. Celtics TV ScheduleAll times in ET. ** Signifies that the game will only be played if necessary.Game 1: PHI @ BOS, Sunday, April 19, 1:00 p.m. on ABC (STREAM)Game 2: PHI @ BOS, Tuesday, April 21, 7:00 p.m. on NBCSN (STREAM)Game 3: BOS @ PHI, Friday, April 24, 7:00 p.m. on Prime (STREAM)Game 4: BOS @ PHI, Sunday, April 26, 7:00 p.m. on NBC (STREAM)Game 5**: PHI @ BOS, Tuesday, April 28Game 6**: BOS @ PHI, Thursday, April 30Game 7**: PHI @ BOS, Saturday, May 2What to know for 76ers vs. CelticsBoston and Philadelphia split the four games they played against one another this season, though none of those games were played when Jayson Tatum was healthy. Since returning from his Achilles injury on March 6, Tatum has played 16 games. He averaged 21.8 points, 10 rebounds and 5.3 assists in those games. In the month of April (past five games), Tatum averaged 23.6 points, 12 rebounds and 7.8 assists per game. While Boston gets its superstar back, former 76ers MVP Joel Embiid is out indefinitely with appendicitis, which required surgery. In his absence, much of the weight of Philadelphia’s offense will be on Tyrese Maxey. The 25-year-old averaged 28.3 points per game during the regular season, fifth-most in the NBA. Paul George has also been a steady presence for the 76ers since he returned from a 25-game suspension in late March. Maxey, George and rookie V.J. Edgecombe will all have to step up for Philadelphia to have any chance against the Celtics in this first round series.
